coupling_convention: kinetic mixing parameter χ (dimensionless), canonical dark photon coupling
notes: First results from SUPAX cavity haloscope at University of Mainz searching for dark photons. Limit set at single frequency f₀ = 8303.06 MHz (m_A' = 34.34 µeV) from 126 minutes of data at 4.2 K. Reported limit χ < (6.20 ± 3.15(exp.) ± 9.65(SG)) × 10⁻¹⁴ at 95% CL includes experimental and Savitzky-Golay filter uncertainties. Analysis reveals ~80% signal attenuation from unaccounted losses; authors note analysis procedure will be revisited. For fixed polarization scenario, limit degrades to χ_pol < (38 ± 19(exp.) ± 58(SG)) × 10⁻¹⁴. Local DM density ρ_DM = 0.45 GeV/cm³ adopted from standard halo model. Mass converted from frequency using m[eV] = 4.136e-15 × f[Hz]: 8.30306 GHz → 3.434 × 10⁻⁵ eV. | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.75, 30)) | Vision: The SUPAX experiment is a cavity-based dark photon search using a superfluid helium detector. The exclusion plot (FIG. 9) shows the SUPAX limit compared to other experiments (ADMX, IAXO, CAST, WISPDM, Cosmology). The cavity resonance frequency is f₀ = 8303.06 MHz = 34.34 μeV, corresponding to a dark photon mass m_A = 34.34 μeV. The limit is set at χ < (6.20 ± 3.15^(exp.) ± 9.65^(SG)) × 10^-14 for randomly polarised dark photons (Eq. 17). The boundary traced follows the lower edge of the SUPAX exclusion region (red shaded area in FIG. 9), which represents the sensitivity of the experiment across the mass range from ~1 μeV to ~0.1 eV. The plot uses log-log axes with mass in eV on the x-axis and kinetic mixing χ on the y-axis. Data points were sampled more densely in regions of steep slope (low mass, high mass transitions) and less densely in smooth regions. | Calibration: No calibration needed
